newsitem.title: DENMARK: EAC sees 97 H1 result lower than expected.
newsitem.headline: EAC sees 97 H1 result lower than expected.

text.p: Danish shipping and trading group East Asiatic Company said on Monday that it now expected first half 1997 operating profit at a lower level than previously forecast.

EAC said in a statement that a slower than a expected recovery in the economy and purchasing power in Venezuela and failure of its consumer products unit to improve its result in China were the reasons for its lower half year expectations.
In March EAC announced a 201 million crown 1996 group net profit, down on 1995's 338 million crown surplus but said it expected "reasonably better" operating profits for 1997.
In 1996 EAC's operating result was 402 million crowns.
The group's first half 1996 profits before tax and extraordinary items was 176 million crowns, with the interim operating result at 182 million crowns.

"Although we expect an improvement in Venezuela and China in the last six months of 1997, it is improbable that advances in earnings in the second half of the year will compensate for the losses of the first six months," EAC said in a statement.
EAC also announced that it expected its share of a liquidated state insurance fund against war risks for shipping to amount to "a couple of hundred million crowns".

The fund, set up in 1949, was built up from government contributions and levies on shipowners. Its liquidation is part of Denmark's 1997 state budget and was finally approved by parliament last Friday. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
